A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GSASR work. All 23 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original super-resolution benchmark results, runtime and memory measurements, and ablations on Gaussian count and reference positions.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds experiments on rasterization ratio, embedding dimension and window size.

M1.justification: As written, the rendering kernel changes: Eq. 2 adds a covariance-dependent Gaussian normalization factor. The architecture, predicted attributes, L1 objective and rasterization pseudocode are otherwise retained. Expanded embedding and prediction-head descriptions do not establish an architectural redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DIV2K and evaluate the same eight datasets, with the same scaling-factor coverage. The new ablations vary model settings within existing DIV2K evaluations; they introduce no new task or data coverage.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain Meta-SR, LIIF, LTE, SRNO, LINF, LMF, CiaoSR and GaussianSR. Moving the RDN benchmark table into the supplement does not remove any comparator.

E3.justification: New supplementary Tables 10–12 introduce controlled sweeps of rasterization ratio, embedding dimension and window size on DIV2K at ×4, using 720×720 images for the rasterization study. Existing training budgets, benchmark protocols and metrics remain unchanged; additional evaluation explanations are disclosures.

E4.justification: The ablation program expands substantially beyond Gaussian count and reference positions. New studies test whether truncated rasterization preserves quality while reducing cost, and how embedding capacity and attention-window size affect reconstruction. These directly examine previously untested design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The retained average runtime measurements and training-loss curves do not introduce a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark, runtime, Gaussian-count and qualitative results are unchanged. New supplementary Table 10 reports identical PSNR/SSIM of 32.01/0.8536 for r=0.1 and r=1.0, with inference times of 543 and 11,862 ms. Tables 11–12 add reconstruction scores across embedding dimensions and window sizes.

T1.justification: Eq. 2 changes from an unnormalized exponential kernel to one multiplied by 1/(2πσxσy√(1−ρ²)), a substantive mathematical-definition revision. The rasterization-ratio condition also changes from r<1 to r≤1. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction recast the representation advantage from attention's larger receptive field to region-level Gaussian predictions, emphasizing learned texture shape and orientation. The central contributions—generalizable image-conditioned Gaussians and efficient scale-aware rasterization—remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds reasoning against making Gaussian count proportional to scale and interprets the new ablations as supporting r=0.1, d=180 and k=12. The original speed–quality and parameter-count limitations remain. Its claim of saturation above k=12 exceeds Table 12's tested range, which ends at 12.

D1.justification: v3 specifies window-based base-embedding duplication, three-layer prediction heads with two ReLUs, and defaults k=12, d=180 and L=6. It clarifies comparator reevaluation and full-pipeline runtime accounting. The abstract replaces the project-page pointer with an explicit code/model availability statement and repository link.

R1.justification: The main bibliography contracts from 82 to 65 entries, largely through pruning broad SR background citations. The BTC discussion and Deformable DETR attribution also disappear. The principal positioning against INR methods and GaussianSR remains, and supplementary reference membership is unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory advantages and several method explanations are substantially rewritten, particularly Gaussian embedding and rendering. Related work is compressed, evaluation explanations expand, and supplementary prose is reorganized. This extends beyond terminology and citation-number edits.

P2.justification: The RDN benchmark table moves into the supplement, while the runtime table moves from amid the references into the experimental presentation. Several figures are repositioned, Figure 2's embedding labels are revised, captions expand, and three ablation tables are added. Existing empirical imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: The new ablations substantiate the rasterization tradeoff, while added architecture defaults and evaluation details improve reproducibility. These strengthen an otherwise unchanged benchmark case. The gains are qualified by the unexplained normalization change in Eq. 2 and the unsupported assertion of saturation beyond the tested window sizes.
